data: Psychology of Disaster Response and Humanitarianism is an interdisciplinary course drawing on thefields of disaster studies, humanitarian aid policy, and psychology. This course will introduce students tothe field of International Disaster Psychology in relation to Humanitarian politics and the intertwinedimpacts that these have on individuals and communities affected by disasters. Through the course, weshall evaluate the defining concepts of disaster, risk, resilience, and humanitarianism, the narratives thatsustain these concepts and which in turn shape policy decisions. From the panoramic view of thepolitical landscape of international agencies like the UN, we shall learn to think with a socialpsychological lens of community and group responses in emergencies and disaster scenarios, bringingthis together in a focused look at particular psychological interventions through different case-studies
